title: Humanoid Robots | NVIDIA use case
summary: NVIDIA describes accelerated systems, tools, and technologies for general-purpose humanoid robot development. Used only to support the compute/control and physical-AI branch as a vendor-positioned component category.

excerpt: NVIDIA Isaac technologies provide an end-to-end stack for training, simulating, and deploying humanoid robot "brains." An on-robot runtime computer, such as NVIDIA Jetson Thor, can run low-latency, high-throughput inference.

title: Jetson Thor | Advanced AI for Physical Robotics

title: F.03 Battery Development
summary: Figure describes humanoid robot battery safety, BMS, cell, interconnect, pack-level protection, and certification claims. Used to justify battery/BMS/safety as first-order humanoid product branches.
limitations: Backs battery pack architecture, BMS, abuse/safety certification (UN38.3, UL2271) for a humanoid robot battery system.
excerpt: The F.03 battery is also the first humanoid robot battery in process to be certified to both UN38.3 and UL2271. The custom BMS includes an array of sensors, switches and fuses to prevent fault conditions.

title: BotQ: A High-Volume Manufacturing Facility for Humanoid Robots
summary: Figure describes humanoid manufacturing, architecture redesign, supply-chain immaturity, in-house assembly of actuators/hands/batteries/final assembly, reliability testing, MES/PLM/ERP/WMS infrastructure, and line automation. Used to justify manufacturing/service and full-stack component coverage as first-order humanoid bottlenecks.
limitations: Supports high-volume humanoid manufacturing, actuation supply scale, and reliability loop; no verbatim on dexterous hands/MTBF/field-service specifically but core actuation+manufacturing+reliability claims covered.
excerpt: BotQ's first generation manufacturing line will be capable of manufacturing up to 12,000 humanoids per year. In addition to manufacturing at high rates, we are also ramping up our focus on robot reliability.

excerpt: Our integrated circuits and reference designs help you create humanoid battery management system (BMS) for monitoring, protecting, cell-balancing and gauging of battery packs.

title: Thermal Management for Humanoid Robots
summary: NMB describes thermal challenges from CPUs, servo controllers, batteries, and motors inside tightly packed humanoid robot bodies. Used to support the thermal-management branch.
limitations: Backs thermal management of motors/drives/battery/compute and duty-cycle impact; motor/joint thermal path also referenced (knee/hip spot cooling).
excerpt: CPUs, servo controllers, batteries, and motors generate localized heat—especially in the head, chest, and leg compartments. Without effective thermal management, this heat can reduce performance, shorten component life, or even lead to system failure.

title: Robot tactile sensing research article
summary: Nature Machine Intelligence reports a high-resolution tactile robotic hand and 600 real-world trials where tactile-informed operation outperformed non-tactile alternatives. Used to support tactile sensing as a manipulation bottleneck.
limitations: Open-access article; supports dexterous hand + fingertip/dense tactile array (10,000 taxels cm-2, 15-DoF hand) and tactile-informed grasp/manipulation control.
excerpt: closed-loop tactile-informed control that processes high-dimensional contact data for precise, adaptive manipulation

In addition to mechanical and electrical safety, additional safety concerns must be addressed, such as those associated with robot-human interaction.

title: Powering Humanoid Robots: The Central Role of Battery Technology
summary: The open-access perspective identifies onboard energy storage as a primary system-level constraint for humanoid robots, citing energy density, power output, safety, mass/volume limits, endurance, and thermal management challenges.
limitations: Abstract is openly visible (full text paywalled); the visible abstract verbatim supports battery as central bottleneck, Li-ion cell-selection trade-offs, thermal safety, and runtime/energy-density constraints.
excerpt: Battery technology now represents a primary system-level constraint... combining high energy density, robust power output, and stringent safety within severe mass and volume constraints. Current lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) struggle to satisfy these competing demands.
